messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired -> Service: infra-analytics (srv_analytics_prod), Incident: INC-8764, Severity: P1, Summary: 502 spikes for /v1/generate. Pager: https://pagerduty.com/INC-8764 :rotating_light:
Anika Gupta: I just got a bunch of DMs — looks like the serving oncall didn't get paged. Was analytics supposed to be paged for this?
Samir Patel: I got the page but it landed on infra-analytics. I'm on infra-serving oncall. PD routing is weird.
Devon Lee: Checking PD mappings now — giving a heads up, could be an alias/rule overlap with the new "inference-api" alias we added last week.
Samir Patel: Reactions: :eyes: Ok please confirm, I'm going to ack to stop noisy pages while we triage.
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-8764 acknowledged by Samir Patel (oncall).
Samir Patel: Running quick PD CLI check:
```
# list services with alias matching
pd service list --query "alias:inference-api"
pd service get srv_analytics_prod
pd service get srv_serving_prod
```
Samir Patel: Output shows inference-api alias is attached to srv_analytics_prod AND srv_serving_prod due to an accidental duplicate rule in the Prod-Alerts policy. That explains the loop / wrong target.
Devon Lee: Great catch. I'll remove the duplicate alias from analytics and ensure it points only to serving. Applying now.
Devon Lee: Commands I ran:
```
pd service update srv_analytics_prod --remove-alias inference-api
pd service update srv_serving_prod --add-alias inference-api
```
incident-bot: PagerDuty reassignment: Incident INC-8764 reassigned to service infra-serving (srv_serving_prod). Notifying new assignees.
pagerduty-bot: New assignees: Megan Torres, Devon Lee (escalation policy: serving-prod-escalation).
Megan Torres: I'm on it — seeing 502 spikes on the Serving ingress from Grafana, p50 OK but p95 and error-rate up ~12% in the last 5m.
Anika Gupta: Customer impact: initial reports from 3 Dedicated customers on east region hitting timeouts/502s. No data leak, this is availability-only. Flagging C-level support.
Samir Patel: Mitigation plan: 1) scale serving pool, 2) fallback to smaller context model if tail latency persists, 3) rollback recent autoscaler tweak if needed. I'll take step 1.
Devon Lee: Scaling now:
```
kubectl -n prod scale deploy inference-serving --replicas=10
# verify
kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-serving
```
Megan Torres: After scale, error rate dropped to ~2% and p95 normalized over 5m. Still monitoring for ~30m.
Samir Patel: PD routing rule fixed in console. I created a follow-up ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4521 — owner: Samir, due: EOD tomorrow.
Anika Gupta: Can we add an automated PD sanity check to our deploy pipeline so alias dupes fail the runbook?
Devon Lee: Yep, adding a CI job to validate PD alias uniqueness and to run on infra config PRs. Putting a note in OPS-4521.
Megan Torres: Handoff: I'm taking watch for the next 30m, will message here if anything diverges.
Samir Patel: Thanks all. Postmortem owner: Samir. Will include timeline and customer impact.
incident-bot: Incident INC-8764 status changed: RESOLVED by Megan Torres. Duration: 7m. Metrics back to baseline.
Megan Torres: closing with :thumbsup: — no data exposure, root cause: duplicate PD alias routing; contributing factor: recent alias change not validated.
Anika Gupta: Adding post-incident comms to the support thread and informing affected customers.
Samir Patel: :+1: Great collaboration.
